{{Snowboarding at the 2018 Winter Olympics}}
The '''men's [[slopestyle#Snow sports|slopestyle]]''' competition of the [[2018 Winter Olympics]] was held on 10 and 11 February 2018 at the [[Bogwang Phoenix Park]] in [[Pyeongchang]], [[South Korea]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pyeongchang2018.com/en/schedule |title=Schedule |access-date=2018-01-05 |archive-date=2017-11-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171105010048/https://www.pyeongchang2018.com/en/schedule |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://data.fis-ski.com/pdf/2018/SB/7071/2018SB7071SLF.pdf Start list]</ref>

==Summary==
Due to a broken shoulder caused by a crash in training, [[Niek van der Velden]] was not able to compete.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://nos.nl/pyeongchang2018/artikel/2216241-valse-start-nederland-snowboarder-van-der-velden-haakt-af.html |title=Valse start Nederland: snowboarder Van der Velden haakt af |publisher=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting]] (NOS) |accessdate=10 February 2018 |archive-date=13 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613085815/https://nos.nl/pyeongchang2018/artikel/2216241-valse-start-nederland-snowboarder-van-der-velden-haakt-af.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nu.nl/olympische-winterspelen-pyeongchang-2018/5127017/einde-spelen-snowboarder-van-velden-breuk-val.html |title=Einde Spelen voor snowboarder Van der Velden door breuk na val |date=10 February 2018 |publisher=[[NU.nl]] |accessdate=10 February 2018}}</ref> Then Norwegian snowboarder [[Mons Røisland]], who was considered a possible medal contender, broke a chest bone and tore ligaments in a crash during practice prior to the finals, which made him unable to compete.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BfC3k9Yj4VQ/  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/BfC3k9Yj4VQ |archive-date=2021-12-24 |url-access=registration|title=Mons Røisland Instagram |publisher=Mons Røisland |accessdate=12 February 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Eleven months after the Canadian [[Mark McMorris]] ended up in a coma, he won the Olympic bronze medal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nu.nl/olympische-winterspelen-pyeongchang-2018/5128292/mcmorris-vindt-medaille-elf-maanden-coma-erg-bijzonder.html?redirect=1|title = McMorris noemt medaille elf maanden na coma erg bijzonder|date = 11 February 2018}}</ref>

In the victory ceremony, the medals were presented by [[Pierre-Olivier Beckers-Vieujant]], member of the [[International Olympic Committee]] accompanied by Dexter Paine, [[International Ski Federation|FIS]] vice president.

==Qualification==
{{main|Snowboarding at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Qualification}}
The top 40 athletes in the Olympic quota allocation list qualified (for both big air and slopestyle, the rankings were combined). This meant only a maximum of 40 could qualify across both events. A maximum of four athletes per [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC) was allowed. All athletes qualifying must also have placed in the top 30 of a FIS World Cup event or the [[FIS Freestyle Ski and Snowboarding World Championships 2017]] during the qualification period (July 1, 2016 to January 21, 2018) and also have a minimum of 50 FIS points to compete. If the host country, [[South Korea at the 2018 Winter Olympics|South Korea]], did not qualify, their chosen athlete would displace the last qualified athlete, granted all qualification criterion was met.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://data.fis-ski.com/media/olympic-games/2018/english-qs/owg-pyeongchang-2018-qualification-system-snowboard.pdf|title=Qualification Systems for XXII Olympic Winter Games, PyeongChang 2018 Snowboarding|date=9 September 2016|publisher=[[International Ski Federation]] (FIS)|accessdate=21 January 2018}}</ref>
